The Premium Tax Credit Extension Act is another temporary patch for a broken system. Permanent fixes, not endless extensions.

Funny thing about “preventing premium spikes”…

Congress keeps rushing in with rescue bills for a crisis they helped create.

Here’s what never gets mentioned:

• In 2017–2021, Congress left ACA risk-adjustment payments unstable for four straight years, and insurers warned that uncertainty alone added double-digit premium increases in states like New Jersey.

• In 2022 and 2023, House committees sat on GAO recommendations to modernize marketplace fraud controls the same controls now cited as a cost driver that this bill promises to fix.

• And in 2024, Congress let the enhanced tax credits drift toward expiration without a long term plan, guaranteeing the very year end premium shock they’re now congratulating themselves for averting.

So yes, affordability matters.

But no press release changes the fact that Congress created the cliff and is now selling the safety net as reform.

And now you know…the rest of the story.
